status_summary: As of 2026-10-08 DHS has not been broken up and no administration bill to do so was found. Congress funded DHS as one department (P.L. 119-21 in July 2025, P.L. 119-86 on 2026-04-30 and P.L. 119-98 on 2026-06-10; the texts of the last two contain no provision reorganizing DHS or transferring components, and Sec. 513 of P.L. 119-86 bars use of funds for the reorganization authority in section 872 of the Homeland Security Act unless Congress explicitly authorizes it after enactment), and Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on 2026-09-25 that abolishing DHS will never happen. One element of the Mandate has an administration proposal: the FY2027 budget request, reported on 2026-04-03, proposes initial steps toward privatizing TSA screening by requiring smaller airports to join the Screening Partnership Program, and Mullin sidestepped a House appropriator's question on nationwide privatization on 2026-06-25. The FEMA Review Council approved its final report on 2026-05-07; a CRS summary does not describe a recommendation to eliminate FEMA or move it within DHS, though earlier council meetings included calls to eliminate FEMA as currently structured. Member bills use different designs: a Moskowitz (D-FL) package of 2026-05-07 with Republican co-leads (FEMA as an independent agency, the Secret Service to the Executive Office of the President, TSA to Transportation), a plan by Rep. Delia Ramirez (D-IL) reported on 2026-06-24 to break DHS into standalone entities with draft language aimed at 2027, her Reimagining Safety Act announced about 2026-09-23 (abolishing ICE and CBP, opposite to the Mandate's single immigration agency), and H.R. 7123, a bill to abolish ICE introduced 2026-01-15. DHS issued reduction-in-force notices in March 2025 at its civil rights office and two ombudsman offices, which the Mandate (pages 164 to 166) recommends restructuring or eliminating; by 2025-05-27 DHS said the offices continue to exist and perform their statutory functions.

timeline.event: Reports say DHS is carrying out reductions in force at the Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties, the Immigration Detention Ombudsman and the CIS Ombudsman, with DHS saying the offices slowed enforcement. The Mandate recommends restructuring the first and eliminating the other two (pages 164 to 166).

Government Executive reports that DHS no longer plans to close the three offices, whose web pages say each continues to exist and perform its statutorily required functions, while reductions in force affecting a little over 300 employees continue; a coalition including Public Citizen has sued (the article does not name the case), and no merits ruling is reported.
P.L. 119-21 enacted; CRS reports about 191.02 billion dollars in mandatory budget authority for DHS across CBP, ICE, the Coast Guard, the Secret Service, FEMA, FLETC and the Office of the Secretary.

Bloomberg Government reports that the administration's FY2027 budget request proposes initial steps toward TSA privatization (a 52 million dollar reduction tied to requiring smaller airports to join the Screening Partnership Program) and a 707 million dollar cut to CISA, mainly from eliminating programs focused on countering misinformation.

Public Law 119-86 (H.R. 7147, the Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026; date shown on govinfo.gov) funds DHS for FY2026 in Division A, the Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026, with ICE and CBP Border Security Operations amounts set to zero in this Act. Sec. 513 bars use of funds for section 872 of the Homeland Security Act (reorganization authority) unless Congress explicitly authorizes it after enactment. CRS describes the law as ending a 76-day DHS-only funding lapse that began 2026-02-14.

The FEMA Review Council, created by EO 14180, votes to approve its final report; a CRS summary (2026-05-15) describes shifts of responsibility to states, tribes and territories and workforce changes, does not describe a recommendation to eliminate FEMA or move it within DHS, and says many recommendations would need legislation.

Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-FL) unveils a DHS reform package with a Republican co-lead on each bill: a Secret Service Transfer Act (Rep. Russell Fry) moving the Secret Service to the Executive Office of the President, a FEMA Independence Act (Rep. Byron Donalds; first introduced in 2025) making FEMA an independent Cabinet-level agency, and a TSA Transfer Act of 2026 (Rep. Tim Burchett) returning TSA to Transportation. The release gives no bill numbers and does not describe replacing DHS as a whole.

Public Law 119-98 (S. 2, the Secure America Act, reconciliation) is approved. Title I appropriates 9.55 billion dollars for Border Patrol personnel and equipment, 7.45 billion for ICE Homeland Security Investigations and 3.45 billion for CBP technology; Title II appropriates 13.02 billion for CBP and 31.075 billion for ICE immigration enforcement; the text contains no provision reorganizing DHS or transferring components. CRS describes the law as ending the CBP and ICE funding lapse of 116 days.

Nextgov/FCW reports that Rep. Delia Ramirez (D-IL), ranking Democrat on the House Homeland Security cybersecurity subcommittee, plans a bill to break DHS into standalone entities including CISA, TSA, FEMA and the Coast Guard, with preliminary language aimed at the start of 2027; the article reports no administration response.

At a House Appropriations hearing, Secretary Mullin sidesteps a question from the committee's top Democrat on whether he supports privatizing airport security nationwide, which Bloomberg Government says the President is pursuing through the budget process.

Rep. Ramirez announces the Reimagining Safety Act, which would replace DHS as currently organized with a new department, abolish ICE and CBP and keep TSA, FEMA, CISA and the Coast Guard; this runs counter to the Mandate's single border and immigration agency. On 2026-09-25 Secretary Mullin responds that abolishing DHS will never happen (no bill number found).

The budget details come from a Bloomberg Government summary read in part (the article is partly paywalled); the budget document itself was not read. The FEMA Review Council final report was not read directly; the CRS Insight summary does not address FEMA's location within DHS. Bill numbers and committee status of the Moskowitz and Ramirez bills were not retrieved, and the Ramirez item is described both as a plan with 2027 language (June 2026) and as an announced bill (September 2026). The outcome of Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights v. DHS was not found. Not found in searches (DHS reorganization with TSA, CISA and Coast Guard; ORR and EOIR transfers; ICE and CBP merger; FEMA Review Council): any administration proposal to move CISA to Transportation, FEMA to Interior, the Coast Guard to DOJ or DOD, ORR or the immigration courts into DHS, or to merge ICE and CBP. The date Secretary Mullin took office was not retrieved. Public Laws 119-86 and 119-98 were read on govinfo.gov (119-86 through its first 100,000 characters, so Division B was not read); neither contains a DHS restructuring provision in the text read, and the funding-lapse durations come from CRS.
